newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam seeks Hanoi venue for annual donor talks.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam seeks Hanoi venue for annual donor talks.

text.p: Vietnam has asked for its annual consultative group meeting with donors to be held in Hanoi instead of Paris this year so that a wide range of local officials can attend, a World Bank official said on Friday.
The bank, pending approval from donor countries, has agreed to hold the meeting in the Vietnamese capital from December 5-6 ahead of donor talks on the Philippines in Tokyo on December 10-11.
"It's very rare. Only on few occasions in the past decade have CG meetings been held in the object country," the official said.

At the World Bank-chaired consultative group meeting in Paris last December, donor nations and agencies praised the communist country's economic reform drive and performance and pledged to give $2.31 billion in aid.
The official said Hanoi had indicated that it was looking for quality assistance rather than quantity this year because it was being more careful about development project selection.

"So from that point of view I would not expect the general level of funding to go up very significantly," he said. "...from their side they would not be unduly upset if there was even a slight decline."
Over the past three years, the donor community has pledged $6.5 billion to Vietnam, of which about $1.2 billion has come from the World Bank.
The main agency for channelling funds to developing nations, the World Bank has proposed disbursing a further $500 million in soft loans each year between 1997 and 1999.

However, the rate of aid absorption has been slow. The World Bank has disbursed about $180 million and the donor community as a whole has disbursed roughly $120 million, $250 million and $650 million in the three years from 1994 to 1996.
